facts.raw_span: An 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma (cT1N0M0)
was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
new bilateral infiltrative shadows
He reported fever and dyspnea
elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

Serologic testing for anti–nuclear antigen, anti–aminoacyl–tRNA synthetase, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, anti-Sjögren’s-syndrome-related antigen A and B, and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antigen antibodies were all negative
no history of antigen exposure
grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis was suspected
bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33

concepts.why: The patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and symptoms consistent with pneumonitis after receiving ipilimumab and nivolumab, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes.
The patient did not respond to methylprednisolone and prednisolone treatment, indicating steroid-refractory disease.
The patient was diagnosed with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, which is a type of cancer.
The patient developed ICI-induced pneumonitis, which is an immune-related adverse event.
The patient had elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes, indicating an inflammatory response.
The patient had negative serologic testing for various autoimmune antibodies, but the clinical presentation is consistent with an autoimmune disorder.

It explains the negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR, as well as the negative serologic testing for various autoantibodies, which are consistent with a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, a condition that can present with pneumonitis and is often diagnosed by exclusion of other causes.

rationales.F01: Patient's age and diagnosis of epithelioid pleural mesothelioma are not directly related to ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F02: Treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab is a known risk factor for ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F03: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT are a common finding in ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F05: Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels are indicative of an inflammatory response, which is consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F07: Negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR help rule out other potential causes of pneumonitis.
rationales.F08: Negative serologic testing for various autoantibodies helps rule out autoimmune disorders.
rationales.F10: Clinical suspicion of grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis is based on the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.
rationales.F12: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showing a high percentage of lymphocytes is consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient was diagnosed with grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis and showed no improvement after two courses of methylprednisolone, indicating steroid-refractory disease.
